paper_title: The Singular Optimality of Distributed Computation in LOCAL
statement: In this paper, we fully resolve the complexity of distributed computation in the KT1 LOCAL model, showing that singularly optimal algorithms can be achieved for global problems. A question that we leave open is whether any problem that admits a O(t)-round algorithm in the LOCAL model, for any t ≤ D, can be solved in Õ(t) rounds and Õ(n) messages in KT1 LOCAL? In particular, the question is whether we can design singularly optimal algorithms for any problem in KT1 LOCAL. This work answers this question for t = D.
context: 5 Conclusion In this paper, we fully resolve the complexity of distributed computation in the KT1 LOCAL model, showing that singularly optimal algorithms can be achieved for global problems. A question that we leave open is whether any problem that admits a O(t)-round algorithm in the LOCAL model, for any t ≤ D, can be solved in Õ(t) rounds and Õ(n) messages in KT1 LOCAL? In particular, the question is whether we can design singularly optimal algorithms for any problem in KT1 LOCAL. This work answers this question for t = D. Another interesting question is whether one can improve the complexities of our KT1 LOCAL algorithms. In particular, can we obtain an O(D)-round algorithm for a BFS tree (or leader election and broadcast) that uses Õ(n) messages? Finally, a major open question is whether singular optimality is possible for global problems in the KT1 CONGEST model.
